prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, a ligand-controlled and mechanistically understood method for constructing aryl amines.

statement.case_for: I keep Pd-catalysed C-N coupling as my first choice after the full round-1 exchange. It is the only shortlisted candidate where generality, mechanistic understanding, three decades of independent confirmation and a two-name attribution all hold together. The decisive evidence is structural and mechanistic: the identified Pd-amido intermediates, the C-N reductive elimination step and the ligand effects (bulky biaryl phosphines from Buchwald, hindered alkyl and ferrocenyl phosphines from Hartwig) are characterised, not inferred, and they explain why the reaction became predictable across substrates. Aryl amines are everywhere in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and organic materials, and the method is routine in process chemistry. On the chair's question, what is distinct from 2010: the 2010 prize recognised C-C bond formation through oxidative addition and transmetalation. The C-N problem was not solved by transferring that recipe. Amine binding, deprotonation to the amido complex, and a slow C-N reductive elimination that competes with beta-hydride elimination needed their own ligand solution, and that is what Buchwald and Hartwig independently supplied. A citation framed around this ligand-controlled catalytic general method is a different achievement, not a second helping of the same one.
statement.case_against: The overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize remains the real risk: members who weigh novelty of principle will read this as an extension to a new bond, and four colleagues said so explicitly. Kosugi and Migita's tin-amide coupling is a precursor, and I cannot verify priority details from the files, so the expert report should settle it before the citation is final. B004 also looks conservative beside lipid delivery, whose medical consequences are more visible, and a single two-name part leaves the third name slot unused without any natural partner among the other shortlisted candidates.

responses.point: Linke asks whether the committee should move its first choice from B021 toward B040 or B004, and prefers Car-Parrinello for its single idea and clean two-name credit.
responses.response: I agree the attribution of Car-Parrinello is as clean as it gets, and the idea is explainable in two sentences. My reservation stands: its reach is largely through descendants and specialist methods, and you yourself name the 2013 and 2024 computational prizes as a recency problem. B004 has the same attribution cleanliness and a much more direct line from the discovery to what experimental chemists do every week. Since no other member supports B021, I would invite you to move to B004, where Somfai and I already have a pair and the alternatives of Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes and Sparr already point. I keep B021 as my second alternative because I do not consider it unworthy.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers ionizable lipid nanoparticles with Cullis, MacLachlan and Anderson, and says maturity is settled by independent validation at scale, though his priority judgment rests on recollection.
responses.response: I accept that maturity is not the issue for B040; patisiran and the vaccines settle that. My concern is that the attribution is open by your own account: you rest the trio on recollection, Chabes proposed Cullis, Madden and Hope, and Aili and Sparr say Cullis is the anchor but differ on the others. Anderson's lipidoid libraries are a screening and materials contribution, distinct from the pKa-tuned lipid and rapid-mixing principle that you cite as decisive. A prize for the formulation principle with Cullis, Madden and Hope would exclude Anderson, and the trio you propose would exclude Madden and Hope. Until the expert report fixes who first showed the principle in vivo, I prefer the configuration where no essential contributor is left out.

responses.point: Sparr argues B040 is a self-assembly and colloid-chemistry design principle, the missing half of the 2023 Medicine mRNA story, and asks which lipid-assembly steps are decisive for endosomal escape.
responses.response: That is the strongest chemistry argument for B040 and it moves me: a pKa-tuned lipid driving a phase change in the acidifying endosome is a real structure-property rule, so I no longer regard the 'formulation, not chemistry' objection as serious, and I ranked it as my first alternative for that reason. Where I still differ is the structural evidence. The inverted hexagonal phase and fusion mechanism for endosomal release is inferred from model-lipid biophysics, while for C-N coupling the key intermediates and elementary steps are isolated and characterised. Given the six-name credit problem you also name, I would not trade a mechanistically demonstrated method with a clean pair for a stronger story with a contested trio.

responses.point: Chabes prefers targeted protein degradation (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) as one induced-proximity principle, but concedes no designed PROTAC is approved and the two lineages may look stitched together.
responses.response: I appreciate that you rest the case on mechanism and the independent reproduction of cereblon work, and I agree the cereblon discovery by Handa is a real molecular-recognition result. But the citation has to cover two discoveries, PROTAC design and the glue mechanism, with Sakamoto, Ito, Ciulli, Gray and Kim excluded, and you say yourself that the clinical benefit is prospective. Ciulli's structural work on VHL and ternary complexes is exactly the structural evidence that would make a designed-degrader mechanism convincing, and it falls outside your trio. I find B046 premature on both attribution and maturity. I note and welcome your acceptance that B004 is not disqualified by the 2010 overlap.

responses.point: Somfai prefers B004 with Buchwald and Hartwig and is asked by the chair to separate the ligand and mechanism contribution from the C-C precedent.
responses.response: I agree on the pair and on the maturity argument. On the chair's question I would put the separation this way for a general audience: the 2010 laureates taught chemists to join carbon atoms; here the bond forms between carbon and nitrogen, and a catalyst that works for carbon does not simply work for nitrogen, because the amine can poison the metal and the final bond-forming step is slow. Bulky ligands were what made it fast and general. On Kosugi, I would keep him out of the citation and have the expert report document that his stoichiometric tin-amide reaction was not a general catalytic method, rather than add a third name that dilutes a clean pair.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers PCET (Meyer, Mayer, Hammes-Schiffer) as a fundamental mechanism, and wants the expert report read before omitting Kosugi from B004.
responses.response: I agree that the expert report should settle Kosugi's role before the vote, and I have said I cannot weigh priority from the files. On PCET, I respect its fundamental weight, but a citation spanning theory, thermochemistry and electrocatalysis is diffuse, Nocera's role is unresolved, and you flag the weak support and your own field proximity yourself. I do not see a single attributable discovery that the committee could state in one sentence, so I do not move toward B066.

uncertainties: Whether a majority will treat C-N coupling as a distinct achievement or as an extension of the 2010 prize; I cannot resolve this by argument and it may decide the vote.
Whether the expert report supports excluding Kosugi from the citation; if it shows a general catalytic precursor, I would reconsider the two-name pair.
Whether the committee resolves B040 attribution to a defensible trio; if it does, I would move B040 above B004 as a second-ballot choice, since I regard it as worthy.
Whether a two-part prize is feasible under the three-person cap; I see no good partner for a two-name B004 and keep a single part.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with B004 or its candidates. My connections are in electron crystallography and porous materials, none of which are in my configuration, and I have a colleague relationship with the secretary at Stockholm University that bears on no shortlisted candidate. I have no ties to the B040 or B021 candidates named in my alternatives.
